lines: Nuxt no longer depends on [`jiti`](https://github.com/unjs/jiti). Files loaded outside the bundler (`nuxt.config.ts`, files in `modules/`, and layer configs) are now imported by the runtime itself.

-**You can still write your config in TypeScript.** Nuxt 5 requires Node `22.21`, `24.11` or later, where type stripping is on by default, so `nuxt.config.ts` and TypeScript modules load natively. Two things the runtime does not do, which `jiti` used to paper over, are guess file extensions and compile TypeScript syntax that emits code.

+**You can still write your config in TypeScript.** Nuxt 5 requires Node `22.22`, `24.11` or later, where type stripping is on by default, so `nuxt.config.ts` and TypeScript modules load natively. Two things the runtime does not do, which `jiti` used to paper over, are guess file extensions and compile TypeScript syntax that emits code.

Both would otherwise only surface when Nuxt loads the file, so the generated `node` tsconfig now describes the environment the way the runtime sees it (`module` and `moduleResolution` set to `nodenext`, plus [`erasableSyntaxOnly`](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#erasableSyntaxOnly)) and TypeScript reports both up front.

+Route rule patterns now follow the [URLPattern](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/URL_Pattern_API) syntax. A `*` matches any number of segments rather than exactly one, so a rule keyed `/blog/*` also applies to `/blog/2026/hello`. To match a single segment, use a named parameter:
+A pattern can contain only one `*` or `**`, so a key such as `/*/comments/**` fails the build. Replace all but one of them with named parameters, for example `/:post/comments/**`.
+See the rou3 migration guide for the other pattern syntax changes.
+#### Route Rules: Regex Constraints Can't Match Encoded Characters

+Regex constraints in route rule patterns, such as `/products/:id([a-z0-9]+)`, are matched against the percent-encoded path. The build fails if a constraint can match `%` or a character that is percent-encoded in a path, such as `[é]`, a space, `.`, `\S` or a negated class like `[^a-z]`, or if it uses a word boundary (`\b` or `\B`). List the characters a constraint allows instead, or use a parameter without a constraint (such as `/products/:id`) to match any value.
+#### Server Storage Is Renamed to KV

+`useStorage()` from `nitro/storage` is now `useKV()` from `nitro/kv`, and the `nitro.storage` option is now `nitro.kv`. Mounts that only apply in development move from `nitro.devStorage` to `nitro.kv` under `$development`:
+The old names still work for now, with a deprecation warning.
+#### Server File Names Can't Contain Unknown Suffixes

+Nitro reserves dotted suffixes in the names of files it scans in `server/`, such as the `.get` in `server/api/hello.get.ts`. A file such as `server/api/hello.world.ts` fails the build (and is skipped with an error in development) unless the suffix is a known file extension, such as `.json` in `server/routes/feed.json.ts`. Rename the file, or add the suffix to `nitro.scanSuffixes`:

Nitro v3 builds route rules on h3, so custom route rules are declared there rather than on `nitro/types`. `NitroRouteConfig` and `NitroRouteRules` are still exported as deprecated aliases, but they are now type aliases rather than interfaces, so augmenting them fails with `TS2300: Duplicate identifier`.
